messages.subject: Summary statistics from map ped files
messages.subject_clean: Summary statistics from map ped files
messages.body_plain:
Hi Michel,

Sorry if the question is too basic. I am new to this. So in order to run GenomicSEM I need the GWAS summary, I have some data that I plan to use as an exercise. How can I get from the map ped files to summary data using plink? Or can this be done using the munge function?

Thanks,
luis
​

messages.subject: userGWAS NA values in output
messages.body_plain:
Hello!

Apologies if this is glaringly obvious, I am attempting a genomic SEM using the same sample of around 4,000 individuals using 3 separate GWAS, with around 6mill SNPs in each set. This has resulted in memory issues so have broken the data down by chromosome. I initially ran the addSNPs and userGWAS separately but have since tried the combined steps of userGWAS with and without the addSNPs output (Output = addSNPs and Output = NULL). For the first 100 SNPs, the following occurs:

modelCh1<-"F1 =~ NA*Var1 + Var2 + Var3

F1 ~~1*F1

Var1 ~~ a*Var1

a > .01

F1~SNP"

sub1<-"F1~SNP"

SNPSE<-.005

#### Output = NULL

> GWASfactor_ch1<-userGWAS(covstruc = LDSCoutput, SNPs = pSumstats2, estimation = "DWLS",

+                       model =  modelCh1, modelchi = F, printwarn = T, sub = sub1,

+                       SNPSE = SNPSE, parallel = T, Output = NULL)

> #print the first five rows of the userGWAS output

... Followed by same output.

This even occurs when my model constrains the variance (a > .01). Any idea where I might be going wrong and why the values are all NA?

Secondly, just wanted to see if anyone else was having problems with updated/newer versions of R?

Previously, I could only use the package without any updates, but it now results in the same error with/without updates: "ERROR: unable to collate and parse R files for package ‘GenomicSEM’ " ... This has prevented me from trying covstruc = NULL, SNPs = NULL, Output = addSNPs (pSNPs2)

Any suggestions very welcome, thanks very much in advance!!

Best wishes,

Laurel Woodridge

messages.subject: Re: userGWAS NA values in output
messages.body_plain:
HI

so just to be clear did you get the NA's before the update or not?

if its not the update (which it could be) then its either the low sample size (4.000 is very low for LD score regression or genomicSEM) or something about the specific sumstat you are using.

Things I would do to figure out whats going on would include: running the model wthout SNP to see if that does work (because if the model already causes problems then we may be looking at the wrong issue here) then I would move on too fitting the model for 1 SNP.

its much easier to help solve this if you save your R workspace for a trial run of say 10-100 SNPs and email it to us/me:

m.g.nivard [at] gmail.com <http://gmail.com>

Best,
Michel

messages.subject_clean: Summary statistics from map ped files
messages.body_plain:
Hi Luis,

You can get GWAS summary statistics from many sources see bottom of this page for some of those sources: https://github.com/MichelNivard/GenomicSEM/wiki/2.-Important-resources-and-key-information

Now if you want to know how to use plink to run a GWAS than this article is a good start: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC6001694

Best,
Michel
